It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== History ==
The founding year is unknown.

According to Meiji-era shrine registers, it was also called Benzaiten. It is said that the precincts were originally large, about 200 m square, with a pond surrounding them. In 1911 (Meiji 44), it was merged into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamo Shrine}}; in 1922 (Taishō 11), local parishioners built a small shrine again at the present site.

It is an old shrine considered to correspond to the Shikinaisha Yokota Shrine. The ''{{ill|Awa-shi|Q65291985|qid=Q65291985}}'' states: "Yokota no Hokora is the Engishiki small shrine. Now abolished, it remains in Yokota, Kamo Village."

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ichikishimahime no Mikoto}}

== Access ==
* About 10 minutes on foot from {{ill|Awa-Kamo Station|Q4829611|qid=Q4829611}} on the {{ill|Tokushima Line|Q899310|qid=Q899310}} of {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|Q496531|qid=Q496531|lt=JR}}.
